title: [Concerning Adam]
text:
⟨p.157⟩
{0} {1} Adam — 91
Once again he said to his disciples who hear his
words, saying: Three great works, being altered, have manifested
forth in {2}, the First Man. For this reason there belongs to him
eternally an exaltation above the powers united, those in heaven
and those in the earth.
The first: that they placed
upon him the icon of the Exalted One. The demiurges
and the molders of his body sealed (him) before the {3} likeness
radiant of the icon, which manifested itself to them from the upper place.
For this reason the icon of Adam exists exalted, beautiful,
more than every power, joined with those above and those below.
The second work: that they molded Adam in his structure
{4} of the firstborn-state of heaven and
{5} the Five Sons. For this reason his
{6} is altered compared with the structure of the rest of the creatures,
{7} the structure of all the creatures is altered. Adam
{8}, the molding of his soul is extended unto the
straight-extension and the spreading-forth of the elements. There is a
Mind in him, exalted above that of the other creatures and
that of the cattle.
The third is the teaching
and the counsels and the seal of all the powers, those above and
those below — which the demiurges who established him gathered, and they
set within him himself with his portion, being arranged as houses
of the zodiac-signs and the stars and the divisions of the days and the
years. Since the seal of the entire cosmos is sealed in
Adam, for this reason heaven and earth move on his account, they
are disturbed, and a turmoil comes to be on his occasion: both the
beautiful and the bitter ones. The beautiful indeed are drawn unto life
because of their icon and their form which is set upon him; the
{9}bitter themselves are drawn unto death — that they may exercise authority
{10} in him, and take precedence in the kingship, and abase in him
{11} entire.
Once again truly: that the
{12} appointed Adam (and) fashioned him, that they may be lord
{13} of the kingship. Concerning seven matters
⟨p.158⟩
The first: that he became an Illuminator (φωστήρ) in their creation, in place of the
light of the icon of the Ambassador, which he revealed to them
forth from above; {0} they all desired
the likeness of the icon of the Ambassador — their heart
drew after her.
The second: that they shall draw
from him the Light, and they shall ensnare him, and they shall hinder him
in his going up to the Height.
The third: that on account of the icon of the Ambas-
sador which is set upon him, the entire godhood shall humble itself
for them — that of above and that of below — on account of the likeness of the Radiance of
the beauty of his lust, for he is desire-arousing in his likeness be-
yond all creatures.
The fourth: that {1} a
imprint-figure of seal and a new character, in order {2}
all the begettings which they shall beget shall be begotten before his {3}.
The fifth: that there shall be revealed in him all the arts (τέχναι)
of the powers of those above and those below, those that are hidden and those
that are revealed forth, and they shall discriminate (διακρίνειν) in him the All; for of every-
thing there is revelation upon him.
The sixth: that a great patronage (πατρωνία) shall come to be for them
in the icon of the Most High that is set upon him; that those of above shall
{4} the other archons, and shall not do any evil to them on account of Adam.
The seventh: that he shall be head and king and lord over the creatures
all, and they shall receive the kingship in him.

lines.coptic: ⲡⲙⲁⲍⲥⲁⲱϥ̄ ⲭⲉ ⲉϥⲁⲣ̄ ⲁⲡⲉ ⲍⲓ ⲣ̄ⲣⲟ ⲍⲓ ⲭⲁ̣ⲓⲥ ⲁⲭⲛ̄ ⲛ̄ⲥⲱⲛⲧ̄
lines.english: The seventh: that he shall be head and king and lord over the creatures

lines.coptic: ⲧⲏⲣⲟⲩ ⲛ̄ⲥⲉⲭ̣ⲓⲟⲩⲱ ⲛⲍⲏⲧϥ ⲛ̄ⲧⲙⲛ̄ⲧⲣ̄ⲣⲟ
lines.english: all, and they shall receive the kingship in him.
